page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an Intel Xeon 2388G processor with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly with the server, consisting of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU scoring 2503.49 (top 25%) and single-threaded gzip compression reaching a top-tier 36.27 GB/sec (top 10%). Passmark memory score is also in the top tier at 3390.33. However, multi-core performance and database operations fall into the average category, with a Passmark CPU score of 23271.22 and Redis SET operations at 16.84 million operations per second. A key tradeoff is memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, which registers in the bottom 25% for both read (36.93 GB/sec) and write (19.38 GB/sec) operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density with dedicated CPU allocation and substantial local NVMe storage, eliminating virtualization overhead. The combination of high single-core performance, large memory capacity, and fast local NVMe storage makes this server well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, static web serving, and single-threaded compression tasks.
